liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hey Pocky Way** (3 reviews): Reviewer hears the opener as polished by now; Steady opener; an odd husky, deep voice appears around 2:00 in the second chorus [16][18][20]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jerry's rocking side is on display in a well-played version [18]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Reviewer's favorite Row Jimmy, with a flawless Jerry solo and a well-judged, not-too-slow pace [21]
- **When I Paint My Masterpiece** (1 review): Slow tempo, but Jerry's guitar playing more than compensates [18]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): Reviewer notes the rare Dupree's in the first set [16]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer recalls the most intense Terrapin witnessed: the closing jam repeatedly builds up and drops back, with audible crowd cheering [17]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer finds Jerry's vocals on Peter deeply soulful and emotional [12]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Reviewer feels Jerry, and maybe Brent, seemed to forget how to play it [20]

## The recordings

- **gd87-11-07.sbd.gardner.9242.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 4.54/5 by 13 [1]
- **gd1987-11-07.sbd-pcm.remaster.uhclem.27581.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [5]
- **gd1987-11-07.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83998.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Sound quality improves during Hey Pocky Way [6]
- **gd1987-11-07.166970.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 144 min [8]

## Around the show

- Crowd was exceptionally fired up; a long Not Fade Away chant brought the band back for the Knockin' encore [10]
- Fans stomped, shouted and clapped about five minutes after the first encore, drawing the band out for a Saturday Night closer [10]
- Band returned for a second encore after the house lights had already come up; reviewer stood at Phil's feet [11]
- After the show, reviewer's friend talked with Healy at the board while the venue emptied to crew and a few fans [11]
- Reviewer saw the band return for a second encore, the only time they witnessed it; venue was enjoyable and it was harvest time [14]
- A We Want Phil chant occurs after Dupree's Diamond Blues and before Box Of Rain [8]
- Much hotter than the previous night, when the band seemed to want to be home [14]
- Unlike the reviewer's wariness of late-80s Uncle John's>Playin'>Terrapin sets, this one is strong [16]
- Better than the night before but reviewer finds it fairly standard, with weak song transitions [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd87-11-07.sbd.gardner.9242.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > PCM > CDR [1]. Also: Soundboard to PCM, via Sony PCM 601ES and RME Hammerfall into Soundforge, then CDR by Sean Weber-small; Bill Gardner turned the CDR into SHN using EAC; the notes mention editing [1]
- **gd1987-11-07.sbd-pcm.remaster.uhclem.27581.sbeok.flac16**: source: SBD > PCM > CDR [5]. Also: Uhclem's 2004 edits removed the fade between disc 2 and disc 3, making those tracks seamless; Also applied DC offset correction to each set, retracked discs 2 and 3, and compressed to FLAC [5]
- **gd1987-11-07.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83998.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [6]. Also: Derived from an SBD-PCM-CD source (shnid 9242), with the encore placed at the end of set one to fit two discs [6]
- **gd1987-11-07.166970.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S90) [8]. Also: The same audience source supplies the second-encore One More Saturday Night [8]

## Art and photos
